title: उदयपुर गाँजा बरामद प्रकरण : परिमाणदेखि समयक्रमसम्म बाझिए सुरक्षा निकायका विवरण
content:
जनकपुरधाम । कात्तिक १५ गते साँझ करिब साढे ४ बजे उदयपुरको बेलका नगरपालिका-८, दिवाजोरमा गाँजा बोकेको एउटा ट्रक सुरक्षाकर्मीको नियन्त्रणमा पर्‍यो। ट्रकमा ठूलो परिमाणमा गाँजा रहेको सूचना सुरक्षा निकायका उच्च अधिकारीहरूसम्म पुगिसकेको थियो। भोलिपल्ट (कात्तिक १६ गते) दिउँसोसम्म पनि आधिकारिक विवरण सार्वजनिक नभएपछि नेपाल प्रेसले सोधिखोजी गरेको थियो । सशस्त्र प्रहरी बलले भोलिपल्ट मात्रै ट्रकबाट ७ हजार ८२६ किलो ८०० ग्राम (करिब ७.८ टन) गाँजा बरामद भएको विज्ञप्ति जारी गर्‍यो। यद्यपि, ट्रक नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको समय, त्यसलाई सम्बन्धित कार्यालयसम्म पुर्‍याउन लागेको अवधि, गाँजाको वास्तविक परिमाण र तस्करहरू उम्किएको घटनाक्रमले सुरक्षा निकायको भूमिकामाथि गम्भीर प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ। स्रोतले ट्रकमा करिब १३ हजार किलो (१३ टन) गाँजा रहेको दाबी गरिरहँदा सशस्त्रले सार्वजनिक गरेको परिमाण र स्रोतको दाबीबीच झन्डै ५ टनको अन्तर देखिएको छ । सशस्त्र प्रहरी बलका सहप्रवक्ता डीएसपी शैलेन्द्र थापाका अनुसार विशेष सूचनाका आधारमा इन्टेलिजेन्स ब्युरो, नं. ४ गण सुनसरी र नं. ५ गण उदयपुरको संयुक्त टोलीले बेलका–८ स्थित मैनामैनी–कोशीपुल भित्री सडकखण्डमा जाँच गरेको थियो। त्यस क्रममा प्रदेश १–०२–००२ ख ०२०६ नम्बरको १२ चक्के ट्रकमा २४६ वटा प्लास्टिकका बोरामा लुकाइछिपाइ राखिएको ७ हजार ८२६ किलो ८०० ग्राम गाँजा फेला परेको र ट्रकसहित गाँजा आवश्यक कारबाहीका लागि नेपाल प्रहरीलाई बुझाउने प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइएको सशस्त्रले जनाएको छ। नेपाल प्रेसलाई प्राप्त जानकारीअनुसार उक्त ट्रक नियन्त्रणमा लिनुअघि नै ठूलो परिमाणमा गाँजा ओसारपसार भइरहेको सूचना सशस्त्र प्रहरी कोशी प्रदेशका डीआईजी मनिष थापा र कोशी प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालयका डीआईजी शेखर खनालसम्म पुगेको थियो। नेपाल प्रहरीका डीआईजी खनालले पनि गाँजा ओसारपसार भइरहेको सूचना पाएर टोली खटाएको पुष्टि गरे। उनले भने, “सूचना मलाई पनि आएको थियो, हामीले पनि टोली खटाएका थियौँ। तर सशस्त्र प्रहरीको टोलीले ट्रक नियन्त्रणमा लियो।” यद्यपि, पूर्वसूचना हुँदाहुँदै नेपाल प्रहरीको तर्फबाट के कस्तो पूर्वतयारी गरिएको थियो र नियन्त्रणपछि जिम्मेवारी कसरी हस्तान्तरण भयो भन्नेबारे उनले विस्तृत खुलाएनन्। स्रोतका अनुसार सशस्त्र प्रहरीको रामपुर बेस क्याम्पबाट खटिएको टोलीले कोशीपारि सडकखण्डमा चेकिङ राखेको थियो । गाँजा लोड गरिएको ट्रकलाई केही व्यक्तिहरूले मोटरसाइकलबाट ‘स्कर्टिङ’ गरिरहेका थिए। चेकिङ देखेपछि ट्रकलाई फर्काउने क्रममा प्रहरीले फेला पारेको बताइए पनि चालक र स्कर्टिङमा संलग्न व्यक्तिहरू भने फरार भए। पूर्वसूचना र घेराबन्दीका बाबजुद मुख्य अभियुक्तहरू कसरी उम्कन सफल भए भन्ने विषय शंकाको घेरामा छ। डीआईजी र इन्स्पेक्टरका बाझिएका तर्क ट्रक नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको समय र त्यसलाई कार्यालयसम्म ल्याउन लागेको समयावधिबारे सुरक्षा अधिकारीहरूका जवाफ आपसमै मेल खाँदैनन्। कात्तिक १६ गते बिहान ११ बजे सशस्त्र प्रहरीका प्रदेश प्रमुख (डीआईजी) मनिष थापालाई सम्पर्क गर्दा उनले ट्रक ल्याउने काम भइरहेको बताएका थिए। उनका अनुसार कात्तिक १५ गते साँझ ५ बजेर २२ मिनेटमा नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको उक्त ट्रक बाटोमा हिलोमा फसेका कारण ल्याउन ढिलाइ भएको थियो। तर, इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय रामपुरका इन्स्पेक्टर अश्मिन दोलाङले भने बाटो साँघुरो भएका कारण ट्रक ल्याउन समस्या भएको दाबी गरे। उनका अनुसार साँघुरो बाटोमा ट्रक छाडेर चालक फरार भएको र बिहान स्काभेटर प्रयोग गरेर मात्रै ट्रक निकालिएको थियो। यसरी एउटै घटनामा सशस्त्रका डीआईजीले ‘हिलोमा फसेको’ बताउँदा नेपाल प्रहरीका इन्स्पेक्टरले ‘साँघुरो बाटोका कारण स्काभेटर प्रयोग गर्नुपरेको’ विरोधाभासी तर्क गरेका छन्। ट्रक नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको भनिएको दिवाजोर क्षेत्रदेखि सशस्त्र प्रहरीको रामपुर बेस क्याम्पसम्मको दूरी सामान्यतया अधिकतम दुई घण्टाको मात्रै हो। तर, साँझ नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको भनिएको ट्रक भोलिपल्ट बिहान मात्रै इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय बेलकामा ल्याइएको थियो। ट्रक कहाँ अड्किएको थियो, स्काभेटर कहिले प्रयोग गरियो र घटनास्थल मुचुल्का कुन समयमा कसको रोहबरमा उठाइयो भन्ने विवरण दुवै निकायले स्पष्ट पारेका छैनन्। परिमाणमा किन यति ठूलो अन्तर ? नेपाल प्रेसको स्रोतका अनुसार अशोक लेल्यान्डको १२ चक्के उक्त ट्रकमा करिब १३ हजार किलो गाँजा लोड गरिएको थियो। तर, सशस्त्र प्रहरीले भने ७ हजार ८२६ किलो मात्रै सार्वजनिक गर्‍यो। करिब ५ टन गाँजाको हिसाब नदेखिनु, नियन्त्रणमा लिएको रातभर मुचुल्का र विवरण गोप्य राखिनु तथा अधिकारीहरूका भनाइ आपसमै बाझिनुले बरामद परिमाणमै फेरबदल गरिएको त होइन भन्ने आशंकालाई बल पुर्‍याएको छ। स्रोतका अनुसार पहाडी जिल्लाहरूबाट संकलन गरिएको यस्तो गाँजा उदयपुर, सप्तरी र सिरहाका विभिन्न ट्रान्जिट हुँदै सीमापारि भारतसम्म तस्करी हुने गर्दछ। यति ठूलो परिमाणको गाँजा बरामद प्रकरणमा तस्करहरूको उन्मुक्ति, परिमाणको अन्तर र सुरक्षाकर्मीको अस्पष्ट भूमिकाले घटनाको निष्पक्ष र उच्चस्तरीय अनुसन्धान आवश्यक देखिएको छ । Janakpurdham. At around 4:30 pm on Kartik 15, a truck carrying marijuana was seized by security personnel in Belka Municipality-8, Udayapur, in broad daylight. Information that a large quantity of marijuana was in the truck had already reached high-ranking officials of the security agencies. After the official details were not made public by noon the next day (October 16), Nepal Press investigated. The Armed Police Force issued a statement the next day stating that 7,826 kilograms (about 7.8 tons) of marijuana had been seized from the truck. However, the timing of the truck being seized, the time it took to reach the concerned office, the actual quantity of marijuana, and the escape of the smugglers have raised serious questions about the role of the security forces. While sources are claiming that the truck contained about 13,000 kg (13 tons) of marijuana, there is a gap of about 5 tons between the amount made public by the armed forces and the source's claim. According to DSP Shailendra Thapa, Joint Spokesperson of the Armed Police Force, based on special information, a joint team of the Intelligence Bureau, No. 4 Battalion Sunsari and No. 5 Battalion Udayapur conducted an inspection on the Mainamaini-Koshipul inner road section located in Belka-8. During that, 7,826 kg 800 grams of marijuana hidden in 246 plastic bags was found in a 12-wheeled truck bearing the registration number Province 1-02-002 Kha 0206, and the Armed Police Force has stated that the process of handing over the truck and the marijuana to the Nepal Police for necessary action has been initiated. According to information received by Nepal Press, information that a large quantity of marijuana was being transported had reached Armed Police Force Koshi Province DIG Manish Thapa and Koshi Province Police Office DIG Shekhar Khanal even before the truck was taken into custody. Nepal Police DIG Khanal also confirmed that a team was deployed after receiving information about the marijuana being transported. He said, "I also received the information, we also deployed a team. But the Armed Police Force team took control of the truck." However, he did not elaborate on what preparations were made by the Nepal Police despite the prior information and how the responsibility was transferred after control. According to sources, a team deployed from the Rampur base camp of the Armed Police Force had set up a checkpoint on the Koshi River road section. Some people were 'skirting' a truck loaded with marijuana on a motorcycle. Although the police are said to have found the truck while it was being returned after seeing the checkpoint, the driver and those involved in the skirting fled. The issue of how the main accused managed to escape despite prior information and siege is under suspicion. Conflicting arguments between DIG and Inspector Security officials' answers about the time the truck was seized and the time it took to get it to the office do not match. When contacted at 11 am on Kartik 16, the Provincial Chief of the Armed Police Force (DIG) Manish Thapa said that work was underway to bring the truck. According to him, the truck, which was seized at 5:22 pm on Kartik 15, was delayed in bringing it because it was stuck in the mud on the road. However, Inspector Ashmin Dolang of the Area Police Office, Rampur, claimed that there was a problem in bringing the truck due to the narrow road. According to him, the driver fled after abandoning the truck on the narrow road and the truck was only removed using an excavator in the morning. Thus, in the same incident, while the DIG of the Armed Forces said that they were 'stuck in the mud', the inspector of the Nepal Police gave a contradictory argument that 'they had to use an excavator due to the narrow road'. The distance from the Diwajor area where the truck was reportedly seized to the Armed Police Force's Rampur base camp is usually a maximum of two hours. However, the truck that was reportedly seized in the evening was brought to the Area Police Office, Belka, only the next morning. Both agencies have not clarified the details of where the truck was stuck, when the excavator was used, and at what time the incident report was collected and under whose supervision. Why such a big difference in size? According to Nepal Press sources, the 12-wheeler Ashok Leyland truck was loaded with about 13,000 kg of marijuana. However, the Armed Police Force has made public only 7,826 kg. The lack of an accounting for about 5 tons of marijuana, the secrecy of the documents and details of the seizure throughout the night, and the conflicting statements of the officials have strengthened the suspicion that the seized quantity has been tampered with. According to sources, such marijuana collected from hilly districts is smuggled across the border to India through various transit points in Udayapur, Saptari and Siraha. The impunity of the smugglers, the discrepancy in quantity and the unclear role of security personnel in the seizure of such a large quantity of marijuana necessitates an impartial and high-level investigation into the incident.

व्यक्तिहरू भने फरार भए। पूर्वसूचना र घेराबन्दीका बाबजुद मुख्य अभियुक्तहरू कसरी उम्कन सफल भए भन्ने विषय शंकाको घेरामा छ। डीआईजी र इन्स्पेक्टरका बाझिएका तर्क ट्रक नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको समय र त्यसलाई कार्यालयसम्म ल्याउन लागेको समयावधिबारे सुरक्षा अधिकारीहरूका जवाफ आपसमै मेल खाँदैनन्। कात्तिक १६ गते बिहान ११ बजे सशस्त्र प्रहरीका प्रदेश प्रमुख (डीआईजी) मनिष थापालाई सम्पर्क गर्दा उनले ट्रक ल्याउने काम भइरहेको बताएका थिए। उनका अनुसार कात्तिक १५ गते साँझ ५ बजेर २२ मिनेटमा नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको उक्त ट्रक बाटोमा हिलोमा फसेका कारण ल्याउन ढिलाइ भएको थियो। तर, इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय रामपुरका इन्स्पेक्टर अश्मिन दोलाङले भने बाटो साँघुरो भएका कारण ट्रक ल्याउन समस्या भएको दाबी गरे। उनका अनुसार साँघुरो बाटोमा ट्रक छाडेर चालक फरार भएको र बिहान स्काभेटर प्रयोग गरेर मात्रै ट्रक निकालिएको थियो। यसरी एउटै घटनामा सशस्त्रका डीआईजीले ‘हिलोमा फसेको’ बताउँदा नेपाल प्रहरीका इन्स्पेक्टरले ‘साँघुरो बाटोका कारण स्काभेटर प्रयोग गर्नुपरेको’ विरोधाभासी तर्क गरेका छन्। ट्रक नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको भनिएको दिवाजोर क्षेत्रदेखि सशस्त्र प्रहरीको रामपुर बेस क्याम्पसम्मको दूरी सामान्यतया अधिकतम दुई घण्टाको मात्रै हो। तर, साँझ नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको भनिएको ट्रक भोलिपल्ट बिहान मात्रै इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय बेलकामा ल्याइएको थियो। ट्रक कहाँ अड्किएको थियो, स्काभेटर कहिले प्रयोग गरियो र घटनास्थल मुचुल्का कुन समयमा कसको रोहबरमा उठाइयो भन्ने विवरण दुवै निकायले स्पष्ट पारेका छैनन्। परिमाणमा किन यति ठूलो अन्तर ? नेपाल प्रेसको स्रोतका अनुसार अशोक लेल्यान्डको १२ चक्के उक्त ट्रकमा करिब १३ हजार किलो गाँजा लोड गरिएको थियो। तर, सशस्त्र प्रहरीले भने ७ हजार ८२६ किलो मात्रै सार्वजनिक गर्‍यो। करिब ५ टन गाँजाको हिसाब नदेखिनु, नियन्त्रणमा लिएको रातभर मुचुल्का र विवरण गोप्य राखिनु तथा अधिकारीहरूका भनाइ आपसमै बाझिनुले बरामद परिमाणमै फेरबदल गरिएको त होइन भन्ने आशंकालाई बल पुर्‍याएको छ। स्रोतका अनुसार पहाडी जिल्लाहरूबाट संकलन गरिएको यस्तो गाँजा उदयपुर, सप्तरी र सिरहाका विभिन्न ट्रान्जिट हुँदै सीमापारि भारतसम्म तस्करी हुने गर्दछ। यति ठूलो परिमाणको गाँजा बरामद प्रकरणमा तस्करहरूको उन्मुक्ति, परिमाणको अन्तर र सुरक्षाकर्मीको अस्पष्ट भूमिकाले घटनाको निष्पक्ष र उच्चस्तरीय अनुसन्धान आवश्यक देखिएको छ ।

जनकपुरधाम । कात्तिक १५ गते साँझ करिब साढे ४ बजे उदयपुरको बेलका नगरपालिका-८, दिवाजोरमा गाँजा बोकेको एउटा ट्रक सुरक्षाकर्मीको नियन्त्रणमा पर्‍यो। ट्रकमा ठूलो परिमाणमा गाँजा रहेको सूचना सुरक्षा निकायका उच्च अधिकारीहरूसम्म पुगिसकेको थियो।

नेपाल प्रेसको स्रोतका अनुसार अशोक लेल्यान्डको १२ चक्के उक्त ट्रकमा करिब १३ हजार किलो गाँजा लोड गरिएको थियो। तर, सशस्त्र प्रहरीले भने ७ हजार ८२६ किलो मात्रै सार्वजनिक गर्‍यो। करिब ५ टन गाँजाको हिसाब नदेखिनु, नियन्त्रणमा लिएको रातभर मुचुल्का र विवरण गोप्य राखिनु तथा अधिकारीहरूका भनाइ आपसमै बाझिनुले बरामद परिमाणमै फेरबदल गरिएको त होइन भन्ने आशंकालाई बल पुर्‍याएको छ।

Janakpurdham. At around 4:30 pm on Kartik 15, a truck carrying marijuana was seized by security personnel in Belka Municipality-8, Udayapur, in broad daylight. Information that a large quantity of marijuana was in the truck had already reached high-ranking officials of the security agencies. After the official details were not made public by noon the next day (October 16), Nepal Press investigated. The Armed Police Force issued a statement the next day stating that 7,826 kilograms (about 7.8 tons) of marijuana had been seized from the truck. However, the timing of the truck being seized, the time it took to reach the concerned office, the actual quantity of marijuana, and the escape of the smugglers have raised serious questions about the role of the security forces. While sources are claiming that the truck contained about 13,000 kg (13 tons) of marijuana, there is a gap of about 5 tons between the amount made public by the armed forces and the source's claim. According to DSP Shailendra Thapa, Joint Spokesperson of the Armed Police Force, based on special information, a joint team of the Intelligence Bureau, No. 4 Battalion Sunsari and No. 5 Battalion Udayapur conducted an inspection on the Mainamaini-Koshipul inner road section located in Belka-8. During that, 7,826 kg 800 grams of marijuana hidden in 246 plastic bags was found in a 12-wheeled truck bearing the registration number Province 1-02-002 Kha 0206, and the Armed Police Force has stated that the process of handing over the truck and the marijuana to the Nepal Police for necessary action has been initiated. According to information received by Nepal Press, information that a large quantity of marijuana was being transported had reached Armed Police Force Koshi Province DIG Manish Thapa and Koshi Province Police Office DIG Shekhar Khanal even before the truck was taken into custody. Nepal Police DIG Khanal also confirmed that a team was deployed after receiving information about the marijuana being transported. He said, "I also received the information, we also deployed a team. But the Armed Police Force team took control of the truck." However, he did not elaborate on what preparations were made by the Nepal Police despite the prior information and how the responsibility was transferred after control. According to sources, a team deployed from the Rampur base camp of the Armed Police Force had set up a checkpoint on the Koshi River road section. Some people were 'skirting' a truck loaded with marijuana on a motorcycle. Although the police are said to have found the truck while it was being returned after seeing the checkpoint, the driver and those involved in the skirting fled. The issue of how the main accused managed to escape despite prior information and siege is under suspicion. Conflicting arguments between DIG and Inspector Security officials' answers about the time the truck was seized and the time it took to get it to the office do not match. When contacted at 11 am on Kartik 16, the Provincial Chief of the Armed Police Force (DIG) Manish Thapa said that work was underway to bring the truck. According to him, the truck, which was seized at 5:22 pm on Kartik 15, was delayed in bringing it because it was stuck in the mud on the road. However, Inspector Ashmin Dolang of the Area Police Office, Rampur, claimed that there was a problem in bringing the truck due to the narrow road. According to him, the driver fled after abandoning the truck on the narrow road and the truck was only removed using an excavator in the morning. Thus, in the same incident, while the DIG of the Armed Forces said that they were 'stuck in the mud', the inspector of the Nepal Police gave a contradictory argument that 'they had to use an excavator due to the narrow road'. The distance from the Diwajor area where the truck was reportedly seized to the Armed Police Force's Rampur base camp is usually a maximum of two hours. However, the truck that was reportedly seized in the evening was brought to the Area Police Office, Belka, only the next morning. Both agencies have not clarified the details of where the truck was stuck, when the excavator was used, and at what time the incident report was collected and under whose supervision. Why such a big difference in size? According to Nepal Press sources, the 12-wheeler Ashok Leyland truck was loaded with about 13,000 kg of marijuana. However, the Armed Police Force has made public only 7,826 kg. The lack of an accounting for about 5 tons of marijuana, the secrecy of the documents and details of the seizure throughout the night, and the conflicting statements of the officials have strengthened the suspicion that the seized quantity has been tampered with. According to sources, such marijuana collected from hilly districts is smuggled across the border to India through various transit points in Udayapur, Saptari and Siraha. The impunity of the smugglers, the discrepancy in quantity and the unclear role of security personnel in the seizure of such a large quantity of marijuana necessitates an impartial and high-level investigation into the incident.
